deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether the store can be deleted, requires PREVENT to guard against accidental deletion.

force_destroy.description: If set to true, any FeatureViews and Features for this FeatureOnlineStore will also be deleted.
force_destroy.rationale: If true, deleting the store also destroys all FeatureViews and Features; should be false to guard against accidental deletion.

labels.description:
The labels with user-defined metadata to organize your feature online stores.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: It is a user defined metadata for organizing stores and has no impact on security or data.

name.description: The resource name of the Feature Online Store. This value may be up to 60 characters, and valid characters are [a-z0-9_]. The first character cannot be a number.
name.rationale: The resource name is a cosmetic identifier with no security impact.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Identifier of the owning project - no security impact.

region.description: The region of feature online store. eg us-central1
region.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

bigtable.description: Settings for Cloud Bigtable instance that will be created to serve featureValues for all FeatureViews under this FeatureOnlineStore.

bigtable.enable_direct_bigtable_access.description: Optional. If true, enable direct access to the Bigtable instance.
bigtable.enable_direct_bigtable_access.rationale: It enables direct access to the backing Bigtable instance and is a functional option.

bigtable.zone.description: The zone where the Bigtable instance will be created.
bigtable.zone.rationale: The zone where the Bigtable instance is created. It does not require a separate policy since region is enforced via the region policy.

bigtable.auto_scaling.description: Autoscaling config applied to Bigtable Instance.

bigtable.auto_scaling.cpu_utilization_ta.description: A percentage of the cluster's CPU capacity. Can be from 10% to 80%. When a cluster's CPU utilization exceeds the target that you have set, Bigtable immediately adds nodes to the cluster. When CPU utilization is substantially lower than the target, Bigtable removes nodes. If not set will default to 50%.
bigtable.auto_scaling.cpu_utilization_ta.rationale: It sets the CPU level at which Bigtable adds or removes nodes. This controls resource sizing, not security posture. There is no unsafe value to block.

bigtable.auto_scaling.max_node_count.description: The maximum number of nodes to scale up to. Must be greater than or equal to minNodeCount, and less than or equal to 10 times of 'minNodeCount'.
bigtable.auto_scaling.max_node_count.rationale: It sets the highest number of nodes the cluster can scale up to. This is a capacity limit for scaling, not a security or exposure boundary.

bigtable.auto_scaling.min_node_count.description: The minimum number of nodes to scale down to. Must be greater than or equal to 1.
bigtable.auto_scaling.min_node_count.rationale: It sets the lowest number of nodes the cluster keeps running. This is an operational tuning choice, not an access or encryption control.

dedicated_serving_endpoint.description: The dedicated serving endpoint for this FeatureOnlineStore, which is different from common vertex service endpoint. Only need to be set when you choose Optimized storage type or enable EmbeddingManagement. Will use public endpoint by default.

dedicated_serving_endpoint.private_servi.description: If set to true, customers will use private service connection to send request. Otherwise, the connection will set to public endpoint.
dedicated_serving_endpoint.private_servi.rationale: It controls whether the endpoint uses Private Service Connect instead of a public endpoint and a policy should require private access to avoid public network.

dedicated_serving_endpoint.private_servi.description: A list of Projects from which the forwarding rule will target the service attachment.
dedicated_serving_endpoint.private_servi.rationale: It lists the projects allowed to reach the private serving endpoint - a policy should restrict the allowlist shape as a network-exposure control.

encryption_spec.description: If set, both of the online and offline data storage will be secured by this key.

encryption_spec.kms_key_name.description: The Cloud KMS resource identifier of the customer managed encryption key used to protect a resource. Has the form: projects/my-project/locations/my-region/keyRings/my-kr/cryptoKeys/my-key. The key needs to be in the same region as where the compute resource is created.
encryption_spec.kms_key_name.rationale: it sets the encryption key managed by the customer that protects both online and offline data storage - a policy should enforce it to be non-empty so data is always encrypted.

optimized.description: Settings for the Optimized store that will be created to serve featureValues for all FeatureViews under this FeatureOnlineStore
